# Awesome Loop

> Looped and recurrent-depth language models. Each deep card records the loop layout, what the main comparison holds fixed, the paper's results with table or figure references, and caveats taken from the paper. All numbers are author-reported; nothing is converted or extrapolated. Comparison keys: params = unique parameters, active-params = active parameters, flops = training FLOPs, kv = KV cache per token, tokens = training tokens, depth = executed layers per token, wallclock = wall-clock time.

## Deep cards

- [Inkling 2 Mini](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sjy1203/awesome-loop/main/docs/en/tml-inkling-2-mini.md): Open-weight MoE (26.4B total, 3.4B active) that runs the middle 12 of its 24 layers three times with shared weights, released with a variable-loop research twin used to measure how pass count affects capability and CoT monitorability. Layout: L0-5 (6 layers) -> [L6-17 (12 layers)] x 3 -> L18-23 (6 layers); injection depth-attention; KV per-pass. Held fixed: flops; differs: none.
- [Looped CED](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sjy1203/awesome-loop/main/docs/en/2611.13378.md): Loop the CED encoder layers that produce global KV, train with random depth, and keep only the last round's KV. Layout: L0-1 (2 layers) -> [L2-5 (4 layers)] x max(1, Poisson(8)) -> L6-11 (6 layers); injection gated; KV last-pass. Held fixed: params, tokens, kv; differs: flops, depth.
- [LoopDuet](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sjy1203/awesome-loop/main/docs/en/2611.07211.md): Serve looped Transformers with fewer core loops for ordinary prompt tokens than for the last prompt token and the decoded tokens, run the deep tail as a compact batch in vLLM, and lower prefilling depth when the queue grows. Layout: prelude 4 layers -> [core 6 layers] x 32 (OLMo r32 checkpoint) -> coda 4 layers; injection n/a; KV last-pass. Held fixed: params, tokens, kv; differs: depth, wallclock.
- [SMELT](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sjy1203/awesome-loop/main/docs/en/2609.01343.md): With per-token FLOPs, total parameters and KV cache matched, looping the middle half of an MoE Transformer twice lowers loss at four scales up to 54B non-embedding parameters and saves 6.8-18.0% of training FLOPs on the fitted frontier. Layout: L1-3 (3 layers) -> [L4-9 (6 layers)] x 2 -> L10-12 (3 layers); injection none; KV per-pass. Held fixed: flops, params, kv, tokens; differs: active-params, depth.
- [Parcae](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sjy1203/awesome-loop/main/docs/en/2604.12946.md): Constrain the loop's injection to a stable negative-diagonal form, sample depth per sequence, and fit training and test-time scaling laws for looping at fixed parameter count. Layout: prelude 8 layers -> [core 8 layers] x Poisson with mean 8, per sequence -> coda 8 layers; injection gated; KV n/a. Held fixed: params, tokens; differs: flops, depth.
- [YOCO-U](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sjy1203/awesome-loop/main/docs/en/2604.01220.md): Loop only YOCO's self-decoder, whose layers use sliding-window attention, so extra depth costs compute while the cross-decoder's global KV is still computed once. Layout: [Universal Self-Decoder, SWA-512 (10 layers)] x 3 -> Cross-Decoder, shared global KV (10 layers); injection none; KV single-global. Held fixed: params, active-params, flops; differs: tokens, depth, kv.
- [Retrofitted Recurrence](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sjy1203/awesome-loop/main/docs/en/2511.07384.md): Turn pretrained 1B models into prelude-core-coda recurrent models by dropping middle layers and looping a block, then keep training while a curriculum raises the mean recurrence. Layout: L0-3 (4 layers) -> [L10-17 (8 layers)] x Poisson-Lognormal, mean ramped to 4, 8, 16 or 32 -> L18-21 (4 layers); injection concat; KV n/a. Held fixed: tokens; differs: params, flops, depth.
- [Ouro (LoopLM)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sjy1203/awesome-loop/main/docs/en/2510.25741.md): Pre-train a weight-tied layer stack that repeats 4 times, with a learned exit gate, on 7.7T tokens; the authors report that the 1.4B and 2.6B models match dense models of up to 12B parameters. Layout: [whole stack (2.6B: 48 layers) (24 layers)] x 8 in Stage 1a, then 4; injection none; KV per-pass. Held fixed: none; differs: params, tokens.
- [PLT](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sjy1203/awesome-loop/main/docs/en/2510.24824.md): Run loop l of token i in the same forward pass as loop l+1 of token i-1, let later loops reuse the first loop's KV plus a gated SWA, and a looped model decodes at close to unlooped latency and KV. Layout: [all layers, every loop (100% of layers)] x 2 or 3 (PLT-2 / PLT-3); injection additive; KV first-pass. Held fixed: params, active-params, tokens; differs: flops, depth, kv.
- [MoR](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sjy1203/awesome-loop/main/docs/en/2507.10524.md): Routers give each token its own number of passes through a shared middle block, and each pass caches KV only for its active tokens; at equal training FLOPs MoR beats fixed-depth recursive baselines and often vanilla, with fewer parameters. Layout: first layer (1 layer) -> [shared block (10 layers)] x 1-3 per token, set by the router (Nr=3) -> last layer (1 layer); injection none; KV per-pass. Held fixed: flops; differs: params, tokens, depth, kv.
- [Huginn](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sjy1203/awesome-loop/main/docs/en/2502.05171.md): Pretrain a 3.5B prelude-core-coda transformer with a randomly sampled number of core iterations, so test-time compute scales by iterating the core more. Layout: P (2 layers) -> [R (4 layers)] x log-normal Poisson, mean 32 -> C (2 layers); injection concat; KV per-pass. Held fixed: params, tokens; differs: flops, depth.

## Other papers

- [Model Carving: Training Transformers That Optimize Their Own Topology](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27962): Puts learnable scalar gates on every sublayer of standard and looped Transformers so training removes the unneeded ones; carved models reach lower validation loss than dense models trained with up to 1.7 times more compute. Category: architecture/placement; 2026-11-20.
- [GLiDE: A Fast, Calibrated Decision Model Distilled from Reasoning Teachers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26509): Converts Qwen hybrid LMs into single-pass decision models via bidirectional full attention and multi-teacher distillation; checkpoint averaging plus parameter-free recurrent depth (reapplying middle layers) raises the 27B hidden-set score from 71.52 to 73.37. Category: training; 2026-11-19.
- [dLoop: Looped Diffusion Language Models via Recurrent Latent Refinement](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26275): Restructures a pretrained diffusion language model into a Prelude-Loop-Coda design that reapplies a shared middle block before tokens are committed, reaching the highest or tied-highest accuracy on GSM8K, MATH, MBPP and HumanEval. Category: systems; 2026-11-19.
- [LoopedWAM: Looped World Action Models for Elastic Inference](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25595): LoopedWAM loops a shared six-block core in each expert of a robot world action model, and elastic self-distillation lets one checkpoint serve several action-depth and sampling-step budgets; it reaches 96.1% success on LIBERO. Category: applications; 2026-11-19.
- [Fold the Loop: Decoding-Time KV Memory for Looped Vision-Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25369): FoldCache lets groups of recurrent steps in a looped VLM share the group's final visual KV during decoding; on LoopVL it approximately halves prefix KV memory while matching full-cache accuracy on five open-ended benchmarks. Category: systems; 2026-11-19.
- [Late Entry in Looped Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.24576): Late entry lets new tokens in looped language models skip early passes and run only the final passes over a deep context cache, outperforming matched early exit; Wake verification reaches 5.2x greedy-exact speedup on Ouro-2.6B. Category: systems; 2026-11-18.
- [LoopCache: Accelerating Long-Context Self-Speculative Decoding for Looped Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.24301): Proposes LoopCache, self-speculative decoding for long-context looped Transformers that updates drafts across intermediate loops by confidence and rotates loop-specific KV caches; reports average 10.25x and 14.56x speedup over WFD and LoopSpec. Category: systems; 2026-11-18.
- [Simpler Tiny Recursive Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.23677): STRM simplifies TRM to a single uniformly updated state, using jittered-rate exponential moving updates and slow-channel readout; under TRM's data, parameters and compute it gains 3.8 points on Sudoku-Extreme and matches TRM on Maze-Hard. Category: architecture/state; 2026-11-18.
- [Proximal Targets: Training Looped Refiners on Problems with Many Correct Answers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.22737): Proves that a single stored target sets a loss floor for looped refiners (HRM, TRM) on puzzles with many answers; training each pass toward the nearest correct answer solves 98.8% of multi-answer Sudoku versus 2.5%. Category: applications; 2026-11-17.
- [LoopZip: Visual Token Compression for Efficient Looped Vision-Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.22728): LoopZip compresses visual tokens in looped vision-language models without training, selecting tokens by attention from two calls of the same shared layer; on LoopVL-1B it keeps 97.16% of the original performance at 50% pruning ratio. Category: systems; 2026-11-17.
- [InfuseLoop: Cross-Trajectory Latent Injection for Scalable Parallel Looped Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.22426): Adds cross-trajectory latent injection to Parallel Looped Transformers, so each loop aggregates causally available hidden states from later trajectories via attention residuals; this eliminates training-loss spikes and improves validation-loss scaling up to eight loops. Category: architecture/state; 2026-11-17.
- [Latent Fact Composition under Next-Token Training](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.21921): Baton looped transformers pass the intermediate entity to the second loop as a token embedding; trained only on answers, two variants almost solve held-out two-hop questions, but next-token training makes accuracy rise then decline. Category: understanding; 2026-11-16.
- [Déjà-Events: Multi-view 3D Geometry with Event Cameras via Sparsity-Aware Adaptive Gating](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.21302): Distils an event-camera 3D model from the RGB teacher Déjà View, which repeatedly applies one shared transformer block, and gates that block by event density; it has the lowest pointmap error among evaluated event-based methods. Category: applications; 2026-11-16.
- [Efficient Multi-View Generation with Iterative Global-Local Proxy Attention](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.20703): GLPA sends cross-view information in multi-view diffusion through compact proxies and refines them by reusing the same attention parameters within a denoising step; on FLUX, attention runs 2.65× faster than dense attention and reconstruction improves. Category: applications; 2026-11-16.
- [Latent Feedback Is a Compute and Data Amplifier](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.20404): Tests latent feedback, which feeds each token's top-layer state into the next token's input, against compute-matched multi-epoch Transformers; it saves at most 48% of the compute and 47% of the unique data. Category: scaling; 2026-11-16.
- [LoopSkim: Lossless Multi-Depth Speculative Decoding for Looped Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.19896): Proposes lossless speculative decoding for looped LMs in which each loop's readout checks draft tokens copied from the context and only full-depth readouts commit; without training, its speedup averages 1.73x that of LoopSpec. Category: systems; 2026-11-15.
- [When Does Reusing Layers Help Multimodal Embeddings?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.19827): Tests eleven loop designs for multimodal embeddings, proving that under forward-only attention repeated layers cannot make earlier image states query-dependent; on MMEB-V2 an added loop loses 0.46 points, while native recurrence gains +4.23 points. Category: understanding; 2026-11-15.
- [LoopFill: Pipelined Multi-Token Speculative Decoding for Looped Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.19649): A training-free speculative decoding method for looped LLMs that puts multi-token suffix drafts and shallow-loop predictions in one draft tree; average speedup over greedy decoding is 5.85x on Ouro-2.6B and 5.13x on Huginn-3.5B. Category: systems; 2026-11-14.
- [Architectures and KV Replay for Depth-Recurrent Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.19446): Studies how to cut decoding KV memory in depth-recurrent LMs: looped hybrids need frequent attention anchors, and training with recurrent KV replay lets iterations share KV states with performance close to separate per-iteration caches. Category: systems; 2026-11-14.
- [Wireless Edge-Assisted Adaptive Latent Reasoning for Vision-Language-Action Models in Physical AI](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.19131): Uses constrained deep RL (TRPO-Lag) to jointly choose local or edge execution and the latent-reasoning convergence threshold of a recurrent-depth VLA, reaching up to 23% higher feasibility-weighted task success than benchmark constrained RL methods. Category: applications; 2026-11-14.
- [Folding Language Models into Themselves](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.18113): Concertina folds every N adjacent teacher layers into one shared block run N times with low-rank corrections; distilled from Qwen3-4B on 22B tokens, a 2.27B model retains 84% of the teacher averaged over eight benchmarks. Category: training; 2026-11-13.
- [Classical Energies Learn to Reason 1,000x Faster than Looped Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.17309): CRAM, a learned Hopfield-Tank energy minimized at inference, solves 99.996% of Sudoku-Extreme and 100% of Maze-Unique test puzzles with training at least 1,000x faster than looped models; the authors call these benchmarks trivially solvable. Category: training; 2026-11-12.
- [Rectified Looped Transformer](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.16265): Feeds each loop a linear interpolation between the current state and the block's prediction; at matched depth this lowers perplexity versus a standard looped Transformer and keeps hidden-state norms more stable, with no extra parameters. Category: architecture/state; 2026-11-12.
- [One Block Is Enough: LoopMR for Accelerated MRI Reconstruction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.14947): Reuses one Restormer block at every iteration of unrolled MRI reconstruction and beats PromptMR+ with about 1/9 of its parameters; shared transformer blocks match or beat distinct-weight ones, while shared CNN blocks do worse. Category: applications; 2026-11-11.
- [Depth as a Candidate Source: Portfolio Allocation for Recurrent Test-Time Scaling in Large Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.12293): Shows deeper recurrence in a frozen Huginn can lose correct answers found at shallower depths, and proposes Depth Portfolio Allocation, which spreads a test-time budget across depths and expands oracle coverage at matched candidate counts. Category: depth; 2026-11-09.
- [WiFo-R: Wireless Foundation Model with Recurrent Channel Representation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.11275): Builds a wireless channel foundation model whose parameter-shared recurrent updates refine CSI features and add latent tokens; multi-depth pretraining trains intermediate states to reconstruct CSI, and selectable depth improves the accuracy-complexity trade-off. Category: applications; 2026-11-08.
- [Energy-Based Reasoners: Your Recurrent Reasoner Should Be an Energy-Based Model](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.08977): Learns an energy over latent reasoning states and makes each loop a gradient step on it, giving a stopping signal; reaches 99.9% accuracy on Sudoku-Extreme with 345× less inference compute than the next-best model. Category: applications; 2026-11-06.
- [ARC-VLN: Adaptive Recursive Computing-based Visual-Language Navigation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.18696): ARC-VLN runs a shared-parameter language backbone recursively for aerial VLN, letting only visual tokens exit early; on OpenFly it has the lowest navigation error of the compared methods and reduces FLOPs and GPU memory. Category: applications; 2026-11-05.
- [AlterNet: Adaptive-Depth Mixture-of-Experts with Learned Halting for Elastic Inference](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.08741): AlterNet loops over a shared pool of shallow MoE experts, picked by a depth-aware router, with per-expert halt heads for early stopping, so depth adapts and can be cut without retraining; results are preliminary. Category: depth; 2026-11-05.
- [Beyond Quadratic Attention: Separable Gaussian Operators for ODE Vision Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.08236): Replaces ViT self-attention with a separable sum-of-Gaussians operator, globally Lipschitz with fixed kernels, across discrete, looped and Neural ODE ViTs; in the looped setting it raises CIFAR-100 Top-1 accuracy by 5.4-8.1 points. Category: applications; 2026-11-05.
- [Extending Reasoning in Typed Decision Models via Looping](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.07736): RELOAD fine-tunes pretrained encoders or decoders with a damped loop over their middle block; looping improves accuracy and calibration, mostly on reasoning chains longer than in training, where encoders gain up to 23 points. Category: training; 2026-11-05.
- [BRIDGE: Bridging the Semantic Quantization Gap for Generative Recommendation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.07425): For generative recommendation, BRIDGE adds latent reasoning, self-distillation and effort-aware recurrence, which runs a shared loop decoder more times at early Semantic ID levels; it improves Recall@10 and NDCG@10 on three Amazon benchmarks. Category: applications; 2026-11-05.
- [Loopback Transformer: Towards a Unified View of Residual Looped Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.07226): Loopback Transformer reads each shared-block update separately, using geometric decay for total update weight and attention to allocate it; it reaches lower validation loss than standard Transformers with 40-75% of their Transformer parameters. Category: architecture/state; 2026-11-04.
- [LooM: Loop-Invariant Memory for Causal Encoder-Decoder Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.06835): Loops the decoder layers of a causal encoder-decoder, storing each token's KV only on its first visit; one model covers 3 to 21 layer executions per token and, with enough loops, beats a single-pass baseline. Category: architecture/placement; 2026-11-04.
- [Loop Before You Leap: What Recurrent Depth Can and Cannot Buy in Data-Limited Pretraining](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.06206): Compares standard and looped Transformers under a 100M-word budget; text-only, a 12-layer stack repeated four times beats a 48-layer Transformer by 5.4 BLiMP points, but recurrence does not clearly mitigate the multimodal-training drop. Category: scaling; 2026-11-04.
- [Give the Drafter a Second Chance to Guess: Parallel Reconsideration for Speculative Decoding](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.05724): Lets a speculative-decoding drafter deepen uncertain guesses with extra passes of its shared block, run in parallel with the one-pass draft; this improves acceptance length by 5.3% to 10.2% and speedup by 3.5% to 9.2%. Category: systems; 2026-11-03.
- [LoopVQ: Sub 1-bit KV Cache Quantization for Looped Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.05304): LoopVQ vector-quantizes the KV cache of looped transformers, coding channels of several loop steps jointly; with Ouro and Huginn at 0.5 bits per element, it outperforms KV vector quantization methods built for standard LLMs. Category: systems; 2026-11-03.
- [ARLoop: Fully-Open Pre-trained Looped Transformers with Attention Residuals](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.05234): ARLoop gives each layer of a looped transformer attention over earlier outputs across depth; sliding-window depth attention matches full history, and a 1.2B model trained on 0.5T tokens beats Huginn-3.5B on all evaluated tasks. Category: architecture/state; 2026-11-03.
- [What Sets the Serving Speed of Looped Language Models? Measurements and Optimizations Graded by Exactness](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.05150): Measures serving of looped LMs Ouro and Huginn-0125, grading optimizations by exactness; the many small kernels per token set the cost, and fusing them behind rounding fences raises throughput 1.11-1.59x with identical outputs. Category: systems; 2026-11-03.
- [Best-of-Depth: Learning Exploratory Dynamics in Looped Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.04663): Best-of-Depth trains a looped Transformer's recurrent trajectory as a candidate set by minimizing prediction loss across depths; on N-Queens, coverage reaches 91.03% versus 45.75% for final-depth training. Category: training; 2026-11-03.
- [LoopKV: Loop-Aware KV Cache Compression for Serving Looped Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.04137): Chooses 4-bit, 2-bit or final-loop KV reuse for each (loop, layer) cell of Ouro from an offline profile; serving Ouro-1.4B, the LoopKV-M plan stores 35% less KV than KIVI-4 and sustains 1.7-2.2x its goodput. Category: systems; 2026-11-03.
- [Dory1.0-4B: A Looped Normalized-GPT](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.03998): Dory1.0-4B is a looped nGPT language model with elastic depth, pre-trained on 6 trillion tokens; more loops raise accuracy, and caching only last-loop KV keeps most gains at a non-looped KV footprint. Category: depth; 2026-11-02.
- [Library of Layers (LoL): Adaptively Ordering Transformer Layers at Runtime](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.03526): Library of Layers uses a router to choose and order blocks from a global library at inference, covering dense, depth-recurrent and MoE designs; it is competitive with all three when pretrained on text. Category: architecture/placement; 2026-11-02.
- [Solv3R: 3D Looped Transformer as a Multi-view Solver](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.02857): Trains a looped transformer whose update operator, independent of the iteration count, keeps refining multi-view geometry from its current state, so one solver handles offline and incremental reconstruction, relocalization and streaming without task-specific training. Category: applications; 2026-11-02.
- [When Does Adaptive Halting Win? Selection Rules Matter in Looped Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.02333): On a frozen Ouro-1.4B, pre-registered tests show the winner between a trained stability probe and Ouro's exit gate flips with the operating-point selection rule; the probe shows no demonstrated advantage over an untrained KL baseline. Category: depth; 2026-11-02.
- [How Does Chain-of-Thought Supervision Teach Models to Reason? A Theoretical Analysis](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.01740): Studies an in-context linear-regression weight predictor trained on gradient-descent trajectories and run recursively beyond them; long-horizon reasoning has phase transitions in context length and training CoT budget, and overthinking splits into error accumulation and amplification. Category: theory; 2026-11-01.
- [There Is No Free Loop: When Does Looping a Trained Model Pay for Its Inference Compute?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.42030): Adds loops to pretrained Qwen3 and Qwen3.5 models (0.8B to 9B) and compares them with equal-parameter and equal-FLOPs unlooped baselines; only the looped 0.8B model beats both, so post-pretraining loops pay only for small models. Category: scaling; 2026-10-30.
- [Where KV-Cache Error Lives in Looped Language Models: A Diagnostic Study of Ouro and Huginn](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.41825): Studies how KV and shared-weight quantization error changes next-token distributions in looped LMs Ouro and Huginn-0125; per unit of error, values carry 94% of diagonal Fisher mass, but keys dominate measured KL. Category: systems; 2026-10-30.
- [ElTab: Elastically Looped Tabular Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.41819): ElTab trains one looped tabular transformer with supervision at randomly sampled early exits; on 30 OpenML datasets it matches six depth-specific looped models and a 12-layer TabPFN-style baseline with 25% fewer inference FLOPs. Category: applications; 2026-10-30.
- [UpLoop: Training Looped Transformers via Upcycling at No Extra Pretraining Compute](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.41720): Grows a shallow Transformer by copying layers and spends the saved compute on looping a shared middle block, at matched parameters, tokens and FLOPs; the 1.3B model's 22-task average rises from 22.99 to 27.52. Category: training; 2026-10-30.
- [How to Loop Your Transformer: Loop Scaling, Specialization, and Parallel Inference](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.40325): In looped decoders up to 1B parameters, full-stack looping is best at fixed parameters and middle-block looping at fixed training FLOPs; per-loop low-rank adapters help, and a normalization fix recovers Parallel Loop Transformer quality. Category: scaling; 2026-10-29.
- [CopyLoop: Fast Looped Transformer Decoding via Context Copying and Shallow Screening](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.38822): CopyLoop, a training-free decoding algorithm for looped Transformers, proposes multi-token suffixes from repeated context, screens them at shallow recurrent depth and verifies at full depth, reaching 2.98x--10.70x speedups on Base models. Category: systems; 2026-10-28.
- [Deeper Backpropagation or More Updates? Training Looped Language Models Across Budgets](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.38422): Compares shorter and longer truncated-backprop windows for training looped language models at roughly equal training time; the advantage of shorter windows shrinks as training budgets grow, so the preferred window can change. Category: training; 2026-10-28.
- [Compute Has Shape: Self-Morphing the Internal Computation of Frozen LLMs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.38382): SelfMorph trains a selector that picks, per input, whether a frozen LLM keeps its forward path, repeats a layer span or branches hidden states; this gives an 8.06% mean relative improvement on five in-distribution benchmarks. Category: depth; 2026-10-28.
- [Think Twice: The Metis-1.6 Technical Report](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37903): Metis-1.6 technical report on Praxis and Logos, two from-scratch models that run a hybrid Mamba-2 and attention MoE stack twice per token; Logos averages 52.93 across 40 post-trained benchmarks, and the report documents training failures. Category: training; 2026-10-27.
- [LoopFold: Parallelizing Recurrent Depth in Looped Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.35556): LoopFold runs several recurrent depths of a looped Transformer in parallel batches, using a predictor for later-loop inputs and a corrector for their outputs; versus a nine-loop vanilla model it cuts decoding latency by 46%. Category: systems; 2026-10-26.
- [StateLoop: Persistent State for Looped Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.35544): StateLoop gives each token a gated persistent state carried across looped-Transformer iterations and projected back into the backbone output; it lowers Pile perplexity versus vanilla looping, with a gap that grows with trained loop depth. Category: architecture/state; 2026-10-26.
- [Cross-Loop Query Handoff: How Later Loops Redirect Two-Hop Retrieval in the Ouro Looped Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.34639): Transplants attention queries between loops of Ouro-1.4B and Ouro-2.6B; loop-3 queries injected into loop 1 rescue 90% and 97% of synthetic two-hop loop-1 failures that loop 3 fixes, versus 24% and 21% with shuffled donors. Category: understanding; 2026-10-25.
- [Recursive CLIP: Vision-Language Distillation with Looped Transformer Blocks](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.34563): Trains and distills CLIP models with recursive encoders that apply N transformer blocks M times at fixed ViT-B depth; CLIP tolerates substantial recurrent block reuse, though the effect depends on the encoder and downstream task. Category: applications; 2026-10-25.
- [Recency Is the Wrong Axis: A Negative Result on Windowed Deepest-Plane KV Caching in Looped Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.34436): Tests a KV policy for looped models that keeps every loop's plane for recent positions and shares the deepest plane elsewhere; across three models, sharing cost depends on late-loop convergence and position, not recency. Category: systems; 2026-10-25.
- [ScaleRLT: Exact Log-Probabilities and Fast Deferred Rollouts for Reinforcement Learning on Looped Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.34427): ScaleRLT removes the log-probability mismatch between deferred rollouts and the learner's dense pass in RL on looped transformers, using a stop-gradient hybrid that replays the rollout schedule bit for bit and keeps the dense gradient. Category: systems; 2026-10-25.
- [LoopGR: Parameter-Efficient Scaling for Generative Recommendation via Recurrent Depth](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.34157): For generative recommendation, LoopGR alternates a shared generative decoder with a lightweight context updater over recurrent depth and self-distills a low-budget student; it beats an encoder-decoder baseline while reducing model size by up to 52%. Category: applications; 2026-10-25.
- [One Model, Two Paths: Balancing Single-Pass and Looped Performance in Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.33517): Adapts a pretrained model to support both single-pass and looped inference by reusing middle-layer weights, and shows joint weighted losses with frozen-model guidance reduce single-pass degradation while keeping looped gains over continued training. Category: training; 2026-10-24.

## Open questions

- [Does running more passes at test time than in training keep improving quality?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sjy1203/awesome-loop/main/docs/en/questions.md#extra-passes-at-test-time): mixed; Models trained with a sampled or variable number of passes stay flat or improve slightly beyond the training depth, and their gains level off near the training mean. Ouro, trained with 4 steps and learned exits rather than sampled depth, loses accuracy at 5-8 steps. No source trains the same model both ways, so the role of sampled-depth training is not isolated.
- [Where in the stack should the loop sit?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sjy1203/awesome-loop/main/docs/en/questions.md#loop-placement): consistent; Every comparison favors looping lower or middle layers over the whole stack or the top layers, and in layouts with a shared global KV the loop should include the layers that produce it. The comparisons come from models of 1.3B parameters or less, or from runs whose sizes are not given.
- [With training compute held fixed, do more passes help?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sjy1203/awesome-loop/main/docs/en/questions.md#more-passes-fixed-compute): mixed; On language modeling at the budgets tested, SMELT and MoR find two passes better than three or four with FLOPs fixed, and in Ouro the gap to untied models of the same executed depth grows with the step count. Other results point the other way: Parcae's compute-optimal number of passes rises with the training budget, deeper training recurrence pays off per training FLOP for two of three retrofitted model families, and on Ouro's synthetic Mano task more passes of fewer layers win at the same executed depth.
- [Can later passes reuse one KV cache instead of keeping KV for every pass?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sjy1203/awesome-loop/main/docs/en/questions.md#shared-kv-across-passes): mixed; Reusing the last pass's KV works when the model is trained for it or when it is done only during decoding, while reusing the first pass's KV alone costs accuracy unless a local window is added. Looped CED loses nothing with last-round KV under sampled-depth training but fails with fixed depth, Ouro keeps quality with last-step KV in decoding but not in prefill, and PLT needs a gated sliding window on top of first-pass KV sharing.

## Open models

- [Huginn-0125](https://huggingface.co/tomg-group-umd/huginn-0125): paper 2502.05171; 3.5B params; 800B training tokens; passes 32; KV per-pass; license apache-2.0.
- [Inkling 2 Mini](https://huggingface.co/thinkingmachines/Inkling-2-Mini): paper tml-inkling-2-mini; 26.4B params; not stated training tokens; passes 3; KV per-pass; license apache-2.0.
- [Ouro-1.4B](https://huggingface.co/ByteDance/Ouro-1.4B): paper 2510.25741; 1.4B params; 7.7T training tokens; passes 4; KV per-pass; license apache-2.0.
- [Ouro-2.6B](https://huggingface.co/ByteDance/Ouro-2.6B): paper 2510.25741; 2.6B params; 7.7T training tokens; passes 4; KV per-pass; license apache-2.0.
- [Parcae](https://huggingface.co/SandyResearch/parcae-140m): paper 2604.12946; 140M / 370M / 770M / 1.3B params; 11.2B / 29.6B / 61.6B / 104B training tokens; passes 8; KV per-pass; license not stated on the model cards.
- [Recurrent-Llama-3.2 (4,6,4)](https://huggingface.co/smcleish/Recurrent-Llama-3.2-train-recurrence-4): paper 2511.07384; 851,501,056 excluding embeddings (Table 8) params; about 50B (Nemotron-CC-Math-v1) training tokens; passes 32; KV per-pass; license apache-2.0.
- [Recurrent-OLMo-2-0425 (4,6,4)](https://huggingface.co/smcleish/Recurrent-OLMo-2-0425-train-recurrence-4): paper 2511.07384; 939,638,784 excluding embeddings (Table 8) params; about 50B (Nemotron-CC-Math-v1-4plus) training tokens; passes 32; KV per-pass; license apache-2.0.
- [Recurrent-TinyLlama-3T (4,8,4)](https://huggingface.co/smcleish/Recurrent-TinyLlama-3T-train-recurrence-4): paper 2511.07384; 704,708,608 excluding embeddings (Table 8) params; about 50B (train-recurrence-k repos); 26B single phase, 52B two phase training tokens; passes 32; KV per-pass; license apache-2.0.
- [TML-d24-varloop-research](https://huggingface.co/thinkingmachines/TML-d24-varloop-research): paper tml-inkling-2-mini; 26.4B params; not stated training tokens; passes 3; KV per-pass; license apache-2.0.
